question: A linked list has 10,000 nodes and you hold only head. How do you read the value of node number 5,000?
options: Read it directly at index 4,999, like an array
Follow next from head about 5,000 times
explanation: Nodes are not stored at numbered places. Each node only knows its next node, so reaching the k-th node takes about k steps: O(k).

question: Why do many linked-list solutions put a dummy node in front of head?
options: Every real node, the head too, then has a node before it, so deleting or inserting at the head needs no special case
It stops the list from having a cycle
explanation: Deleting a node changes the pointer of the node before it. The head has none, unless you add a dummy. At the end, return dummy.next, which may be a new head.

question: In an in-place reversal, what goes wrong if you set curr.next = prev before saving curr.next?
options: Nothing, the order does not matter
The rest of the list after curr is lost, because nothing points to it any more
The values are reversed instead of the nodes
The loop runs twice as long
explanation: curr.next was the only pointer to the rest of the list. Save it in a variable first (nextNode), then turn the arrow around, then move forward.
